issue:
SQLite: JSON operators are parsed as accessors rather than binary operators, so operands bind wrongly

**Affects:** `main` at [`df5ec1e`](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/commit/df5ec1ecd43b83ac63800bf40b04362c9af0173e) (`30.15.1.dev42`); verified against SQLite 3.50.4. Also reproduces in sqlglot 30.14.0.

## Summary

SQLite puts `||`, `->`, and `->>` in one left-associative precedence tier. SQLGlot parses `->` and `->>` as tight column accessors instead:

| input | SQLGlot builds | SQLite means |
|---|---|---|
| `a.data ->> b.key ->> a.final_key` | `a.data ->> (b.key ->> a.final_key)` | `(a.data ->> b.key) ->> a.final_key` |
| `a \|\| b ->> c` | `a \|\| (b ->> c)` | `(a \|\| b) ->> c` |

`->` has the same two defects, with `JSONExtract` in place of `JSONExtractScalar`. This is the SQLite counterpart to [#8035](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/issues/8035). The open [PR #8063](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/pull/8063) adds a corresponding tier for PostgreSQL and DuckDB, but its current diff does not change SQLite.

## Reproduction

```python
from sqlglot import exp, parse_one

cases = (
    (
        "qualified RHS is left-associative",
        "SELECT a.data ->> b.key ->> a.final_key FROM source AS a JOIN keys AS b ON TRUE",
        lambda node: isinstance(node.this, exp.JSONExtractScalar),
    ),
    (
        "|| shares the arrow tier",
        "SELECT a || b ->> c FROM t",
        lambda node: isinstance(node, exp.JSONExtractScalar),
    ),
)

for name, sql, has_correct_shape in cases:
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="sqlite").expressions[0]
    print(f"{name}: {has_correct_shape(expression)}")
```

On `main` at `df5ec1e`, both checks print `False`.

## SQLite verification

SQLite executes the unparenthesized forms with the left-associative grouping, while the explicitly wrong groupings differ:

```sql
SELECT json('{"foo":{"bar":1}}') ->> 'foo' ->> 'bar';   -- 1
SELECT json('{"foo":{"bar":1}}') ->> ('foo' ->> 'bar'); -- malformed JSON

SELECT ' ' || '{"x":1}' ->> 'x';                        -- 1
SELECT ' ' || ('{"x":1}' ->> 'x');                      -- ' 1'
```

## Notes

The immediate qualified-RHS trigger is in [`_parse_column_ops`](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/df5ec1ecd43b83ac63800bf40b04362c9af0173e/sqlglot/parser.py#L6937-L7003): `->` and `->>` are in [`COLUMN_OPERATORS`](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/df5ec1ecd43b83ac63800bf40b04362c9af0173e/sqlglot/parser.py#L1034-L1064), and the qualified-column branch recursively calls `_parse_column_ops`, consuming the next arrow as part of the path.

The broader defect is the precedence tier. `||` is parsed later in [`_parse_bitwise`](https://github.com/tobymao/sqlglot/blob/df5ec1ecd43b83ac63800bf40b04362c9af0173e/sqlglot/parser.py#L6233-L6264), after the arrow has been parsed as an accessor. SQLite needs a left-associative tier shared by `||`, `->`, and `->>`. It cannot directly reuse PR #8063's `_parse_bitwise` tier: SQLite puts that shared tier above multiplication, so `json('[1,2,3]') ->> 1 * 3` must remain `(json(...) ->> 1) * 3` and evaluate to `6`.

Generation preserves the unparenthesized source, so SQLite reparses unchanged generated SQL correctly; this is a source-AST bug.

SQLite precedence: https://sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#operators_and_parse_affecting_attributes

---

*Investigated with LLM assistance; parser and engine results above were run locally against SQLGlot `main` at `df5ec1e` and SQLite 3.50.4.*
